17 ♠ GTO CRASH COURSE - STRATEGY GUIDE



  the mistake you believed they were -- or when a more
  savvy player tweaks their lines to exploit the mistakes
  they perceive in your game, rendering earlier exploitative
  strategies unprofitable.

  Some of the key takeaways from this lesson are:

  •   Some hands are better for exploiting than others

  •   Small mistakes call for small exploits

  •   Big mistakes call for big exploits

  •   Hands indifferent at equilibrium are most sensitive to
      change

  •   Exploitative strategies increase your risk, but also
      increase your reward

  A technical note on what we mean by “small” and “big”
  mistakes in this context: Andrew explains that when
  our opponent makes a small frequency mistake at
  equilibrium by overfolding, we should boost our bluffing
  frequency to 100%. We regard this as a “small” exploit
  because it is simply a change in frequency. Contrast this
  to the situation discussed when our opponent makes a
  big strategic mistake and folds Aces. We exploit this by
  making a big exploit of betting all our Kings that were
  previously checks.
```

20 ♠ GTO CRASH COURSE - STRATEGY GUIDE


    VIDEO 4


  The A-5 Game
  In this lesson, Andrew
  Brokos introduces his         Coach:
  toy game called the           Andrew Brokos
  A-to-5 game. In this
                                Video Length:
  game, instead of only
                                28:26
  three cards, he uses
  Aces down to Fives
  – ten cards. With the
  expanded deck, this game offers decision points closer
  to real poker situations than those exhibited by the AKQ
  game. Specifically the equilibrium solutions of this game
  offer deeper strategic insights into real poker.

  This video helps you to think incisively about the impact
  position has in making betting and checking decisions.
  You will gain insight into why certain hands in position
  make good value bets, while those same hands out of
  position should be checked. In addition, you will find out
  how and why bluffing candidates differ for the in-position
  player. Based on this information, you will learn how
  position impacts the notion of bluff-catching and why
  bluff-catching is a necessary component of the game.
```
